source.title: Reference-Specific Unlearning Metrics Can Hide the Truth: A Reality Check
source.authors: Sungjun Cho; Dasol Hwang; Frederic Sala; Sangheum Hwang; Kyunghyun Cho; Sungmin Cha

record.tranche_reason: Tests unlearning outcomes using FADE, a distributional-alignment measure different from the claim’s attack-based recovery measures; it also reports a GA example that reproduces a targeted answer.
record.gate_note: The paper cites fine-tuning, quantization, prompt, and probing vulnerabilities from other studies but does not test those attacks. Its comparison of original and paraphrased reference answers is a metric-sensitivity test, not a recovery attack. Table 2’s examples of gibberish and refusals, and the T2I results, do not directly test the listed LLM attack versions.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a metric paper (FADE). It still gives its own direct evidence against Version A on TOFU. After GA unlearning of TOFU-1%, forget quality improves from −20.73 to −5.03, yet the model completely reproduces the original forget-set answers. Scored on the original answers, forget quality falls to −31.05. It applies no relearning, quantization, ablation or prompting attack, so B–F are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that reference-based metrics (TOFU forget quality, UnlearnCanvas classifier accuracy) misrepresent success and reward obfuscation rather than forgetting. No tested LLM or diffusion unlearning method reaches distributional equivalence with retain-only models, and many end up further from them than before unlearning. They propose FADE as the better criterion and hypothesise, without testing, that this obfuscation explains vulnerability to recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses named GA, GD, DPO, NPO, and IHL methods on TOFU; LLaMA3.1-8B is finetuned on TOFU and unlearned with LoRA rank 32 for 5 epochs. Evaluates FADE against retain-only models rather than reproducing a recovery-attack protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Forget quality changes substantially depending on whether original or paraphrased answers are used; results also vary by forget-set split, method, and unlearning epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: No method (GA, GD, DPO, NPO, IHL) reaches the retain-only FADE baseline on TOFU 1/5/10%. GA and GD grow more distant as unlearning goes on; DPO and NPO plateau. Outputs collapse into repetition or gibberish, or become refusals unlike a model that never saw the data. UnlearnCanvas diffusion methods likewise raise FADE (e.g. EDiff about 335 vs retain 0.27) despite UA of 98–100%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearned models are distributionally distinguishable from retain-only models: unlearning produces obfuscation-like output behaviour rather than ignorance-like behaviour.

record.problems: FADE is a proposed distributional proxy, and its diffusion-model version relies on stated approximations; the claim’s listed recovery attacks are not tested. The TOFU FADE values in Figure 5 are not numerically available in the text, though the authors describe their relation to baseline. The direct answer-reproduction example is qualitative and from TOFU-1%.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for cited recovery attacks because they are results from other work, not this study. Omitted the T2I UnlearnCanvas results because they concern diffusion style unlearning rather than the LLM-focused recovery versions; also omitted detailed NLL examples in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5, which illustrate distributional mismatch or output pathologies but do not test the specified attacks.

untested.parts: Resistance to simple attacks. Quantitative targeted-knowledge accuracy versus chance. Methods other than GA on the original-answer probe.
All: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All: no activation ablation or representation analysis.
All: no rephrasing, jailbreak or in-context attack. The paraphrase vs original comparison is a choice of evaluation reference, not a recovery attack.

missing.what: Forget quality from paraphrased vs original answers after GA: TOFU-1% −5.03 vs −31.05; TOFU-10% −7.48 vs −24.15. Original answers keep high likelihood under the unlearned model.
TOFU forget quality and model utility trajectories for all methods and LoRA ranks (e.g. IHL TOFU-10% near-optimal on FQ and utility).

record.verdict_notes: The recovery attacks the paper mentions (quantization, relearning, prompting, probing) are cited from other work, not run here. The verdict on A rests on a qualitative example plus the Fig. 2 forget-quality values stated in the text; it covers only GA. The text gives no numerical FADE values for TOFU.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test attack resistance, and does not directly quantify targeted-knowledge accuracy as near chance. It reports qualitative reproduction of a targeted answer and model-utility results.
No relearning or fine-tuning recovery attack is applied.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is tested.
No prompting-only recovery attack is applied.
No robust counter-method is tested against the listed attacks.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8B
rows.stage_stated: Base model finetuned on the entire TOFU dataset for 5 epochs; then unlearned

conditions.value: TOFU question about Basil Mahfouz Al-Kuwaiti

rows.measure: Whether the model reproduces the original targeted answer
rows.value: Authors state that the unlearned model completely reproduces original answers; Figure 3 gives an example reproducing the original answer
rows.note: The paper also reports forget quality changing from -20.73 for the base model to -5.03 after unlearning, despite this answer reproduction. This is not an attack applied after unlearning.
rows.check: State should be absent, not reversed. A's effect (forget-set knowledge removed) does not appear at all, but nothing goes the opposite way. Measure is qualitative: two example answers reproduced verbatim (Fig. 3). The Fig. 3 caption pairs Q1 'full name' with an answer about books; this mismatch is in the source. Baseline: base model forget quality −20.73.

rows.subject: LLaMA3.1-8B
rows.stage_stated: Base model finetuned on the entire TOFU dataset for 5 epochs; then unlearned
rows.operation_detail: Gradient Ascent unlearning; FADE measured across unlearning epochs
rows.measure: FADE distributional distance to the corresponding retain-only model
rows.baseline: figure only; baseline is FADE between retain-only models trained with different seeds
rows.uncertainty: Shaded regions indicate standard deviation across 3 random seeds
rows.note: Authors state no unlearning method reaches the retain-only baseline; they specifically report that GA increases FADE as unlearning progresses. Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: FADE distributional distance to a retain-only model is a different construct from targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery. It belongs in fits_no_version. 'Absent' is not meaningful against any version.

relationships.condition: LLaMA3.1-8B, GA unlearning, TOFU-1% (and TOFU-10% per Fig. 2)
relationships.reason: Despite improved paraphrase-based forget quality, the model reproduces original answers verbatim. Forget quality on original answers is −31.05 (1%) and −24.15 (10%), showing the knowledge was not removed (r1; Fig. 2 values from text).
relationships.display_finding: Original answers remained reproducible verbatim, with original-answer Forget Quality of −31.05 on TOFU-1% and −24.15 on TOFU-10% despite improved paraphrase-based scores.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: GA on TOFU-1%, example targeted question
reader_labels.reason: The paper says the unlearned model completely reproduces original answers despite its improved forget-quality score; this challenges the tested unlearning-success component, but does not test attacks (r1).
